title: How to Write Work Experience on Your CV: Nigerian Format Guide
excerpt: Master the Nigerian CV format for work experience. Learn to showcase your achievements and impress Nigerian employers with our expert tips.
author: ElevateResume

body.text: Your work experience section is the heart of your CV and often the first thing Nigerian recruiters examine. Whether you're applying to banks like GTB and Access Bank, tech companies like Interswitch and Flutterwave, or multinational corporations, presenting your work experience effectively can make the difference between landing an interview and having your CV overlooked.

In Nigeria's competitive job market, employers receive hundreds of applications for single positions. Your work experience section must immediately demonstrate your value and relevance to the role. This comprehensive guide will show you exactly how to format and write compelling work experience entries that resonate with Nigerian employers.
Understanding the Nigerian CV Format for Work Experience

The Nigerian CV format differs slightly from Western formats, placing greater emphasis on detailed job descriptions and concrete achievements. Nigerian employers typically prefer chronological formatting, starting with your most recent position.
Basic Structure for Each Work Experience Entry
Every work experience entry should follow this proven Nigerian format:

items: Job Title (in bold)
Company Name | Location (City, State)
Employment Dates (Month Year – Month Year)
3-5 bullet points describing key responsibilities and achievements
Quantified results wherever possible

body.text: Nigerian recruiters spend an average of 30 seconds scanning each CV. Make your work experience section scannable with consistent formatting and strong action verbs.
Writing Compelling Job Descriptions
Start with Strong Action Verbs

Nigerian employers respond well to dynamic language that demonstrates leadership and initiative. Instead of starting bullet points with "Responsible for" or "Duties included," use powerful action verbs:

items: Managed a team of 12 sales representatives across Lagos and Abuja
Implemented new inventory management system, reducing costs by 25%
Developed digital marketing strategies that increased online sales by 40%
Coordinated cross-functional projects between 5 departments
Negotiated contracts worth over ₦50 million with key clients

body.text: Quantify Your Achievements
Nigerian employers love seeing measurable results. Whenever possible, include specific numbers, percentages, and monetary values:
**Instead of:** "Improved customer satisfaction"
**Write:** "Improved customer satisfaction scores from 72% to 89% within 6 months"
**Instead of:** "Managed social media accounts"
**Write:** "Managed 4 social media accounts, growing followers by 150% and engagement by 200%"
Industry-Specific Examples for Nigerian Job Market
Banking and Finance Example
**Relationship Manager**
First Bank of Nigeria | Lagos, Lagos State
March 2020 – Present

items: Managed portfolio of 200+ high-net-worth clients with combined assets exceeding ₦2.5 billion
Exceeded annual sales targets by 130%, generating ₦180 million in new business
Reduced customer complaints by 45% through proactive relationship management
Trained 8 junior staff members on customer service excellence and product knowledge
Collaborated with credit risk team to minimize loan defaults by 20%

body.text: Technology Sector Example
**Software Developer**
Andela Nigeria | Lagos, Lagos State
June 2019 – February 2022

items: Developed 15+ web applications using React, Node.js, and Python for international clients
Led technical reviews and code optimization, improving application performance by 35%
Mentored 12 junior developers in modern development practices and agile methodologies
Collaborated with cross-functional teams across 3 time zones to deliver projects on schedule
Reduced bug reports by 60% through implementation of comprehensive testing protocols

body.text: Oil and Gas Example
**Project Coordinator**
Shell Petroleum Development Company | Port Harcourt, Rivers State
September 2018 – May 2021

items: Coordinated 8 simultaneous drilling projects with budgets totaling $45 million
Ensured 100% compliance with Nigerian regulatory requirements and safety standards
Reduced project completion time by 15% through improved logistics and resource allocation
Managed relationships with 20+ local contractors and government agencies
Implemented cost-saving measures that reduced operational expenses by ₦25 million annually

body.text: Common Mistakes Nigerian Job Seekers Make
Mistake 1: Being Too Vague
Many Nigerian job seekers write generic descriptions that could apply to anyone. Avoid phrases like:

items: "Performed various administrative duties"
"Assisted management with different tasks"
"Handled customer inquiries"

body.text: Instead, be specific about what you accomplished and how it benefited your employer.
Mistake 2: Focusing on Duties Instead of Achievements
Your CV should showcase what you accomplished, not just what you were supposed to do. Nigerian employers want to see results, not job descriptions.
**Poor example:** "Responsible for managing inventory"
**Better example:** "Optimized inventory management system, reducing waste by 30% and saving ₦2.8 million annually"
Mistake 3: Inconsistent Formatting
Maintain consistent formatting throughout your work experience section. Use the same date format, bullet point style, and font throughout.

Tailoring Work Experience for Different Industries
For FMCG Companies (Unilever, Nestle, PZ Cussons)
Emphasize sales figures, market penetration, brand management, and distribution achievements:

items: "Increased market share for brand X by 25% across South-West Nigeria"
"Managed distribution network covering 150+ retail outlets in Lagos State"
"Launched successful promotional campaign that boosted sales by ₦45 million"

body.text: For Telecommunications (MTN, Airtel, Glo)
Highlight customer acquisition, network optimization, and revenue generation:

items: "Acquired 5,000+ new subscribers within first quarter, exceeding target by 140%"
"Optimized network coverage in rural areas, improving signal strength by 35%"
"Reduced customer churn rate from 12% to 7% through improved service delivery"

body.text: For Manufacturing Companies
Focus on production efficiency, cost reduction, and quality improvements:

items: "Implemented lean manufacturing processes, reducing production time by 20%"
"Maintained 99.8% quality standards across 12 months of production"
"Reduced manufacturing defects by 40% through improved quality control measures"

body.text: Addressing Employment Gaps
If you have gaps in your employment history, address them strategically:
Short Gaps (3-6 months)
Don't draw attention to them. Use years only for dates if the gap falls within calendar years.
Longer Gaps
Be honest but strategic. If you were:

items: Furthering your education: Mention it briefly
Caring for family: Use "Family Responsibilities" as a position
Freelancing: List it as work experience
Starting a business: Include it as entrepreneurial experience

body.text: Including Internships and NYSC Experience
For recent graduates and early-career professionals, internships and NYSC experience are valuable:
**Youth Corps Member**
National Youth Service Corps | Kaduna, Kaduna State
March 2019 – February 2020

items: Served as Mathematics teacher at Government Secondary School, teaching 200+ students
Implemented computer literacy program, training 150 students in basic Microsoft Office
Organized community health awareness campaign reaching 500+ residents
Facilitated adult education classes for 30+ community members

body.text: Writing Work Experience When Changing Industries
When transitioning between industries in Nigeria, emphasize transferable skills:
From Banking to Tech
Highlight analytical skills, customer service, project management, and problem-solving abilities that apply to both sectors.
From Oil & Gas to Renewable Energy
Emphasize engineering principles, project management, regulatory compliance, and environmental awareness.
From Telecommunications to Fintech
Focus on customer acquisition, technical skills, data analysis, and understanding of Nigeria's digital landscape.
Professional Development and Certifications
Nigerian employers value continuous learning. Include relevant certifications within your work experience descriptions:

items: "Completed PMP certification while managing 5 concurrent projects"
"Earned Digital Marketing certification from Google, immediately implementing strategies that increased leads by 60%"

body.text: Many Nigerian employers prefer candidates who show commitment to professional growth. Mention how you applied new skills in your current role.
Final Formatting Tips for Nigerian Employers
Date Formatting
Use the Month Year – Month Year format:

items: Correct: January 2020 – Present
Avoid: 01/2020 – Present

body.text: Location Formatting
Always include city and state:

items: Lagos, Lagos State
Abuja, FCT
Port Harcourt, Rivers State

body.text: Currency References
Use Naira (₦) for local companies and USD ($) for international organizations when mentioning monetary achievements.
Keywords for ATS Optimization
Nigerian companies increasingly use Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS). Include industry-specific keywords from the job description in your work experience section:

items: For banking roles: risk management, credit analysis, regulatory compliance
For tech positions: agile methodology, cloud computing, API development
For marketing roles: digital marketing, brand management, customer acquisition

body.text: Your work experience section is your opportunity to prove your value to Nigerian employers. By following these formatting guidelines and focusing on quantifiable achievements, you'll create a compelling narrative that gets you noticed in Nigeria's competitive job market.
